finals.recommendation:
Hold. In v1, recovery does not move a team lead that still has live members, on any lane. The lead stays in its own pane on its own account, and nothing sends /exit to it or relaunches it. At the reset our own rail types one continue into that pane: no /exit, no --resume, no relaunch, so the team stays whole. The cross-account team move stays in v2.

Claude Code will not wake the lead by itself on this machine. Its built-in auto-continue, and the usage-limit menu it would otherwise open, both refuse while Remote Control is active. remoteControlAtStartup is true in all 5 config dirs, and the vendor prompt appeared 0 times across 98 limit episodes on 2.1.260 and later. So our typed continue is the only wake, not a fallback, and it has to ship in the same land as the hold. finals.recommendation:
Keep the per-account cap at 8 sessions (KMAX) and do not add a raise that applies only during a storm, including a separate recovery-only setting. Record the ruling with corrected reasons.

The reason on record, "a measured 5-6 concurrent-request limit", was never measured on this machine. It came from GitHub issue GH#62426. The 5-hour floor is also the wrong mechanism to cite, because it limits only one placement pass.

Three reasons hold up on the evidence:
1. **A raise buys almost nothing.** Tonight it would have saved 0 recovery-minutes, and 0 of 12 hook-lane runs parked on the cap. Across all 31 parked recoveries on record, it would have saved about 18 minutes for one session and 0 extra recoveries.
2. **The cap is the only limit that builds up across passes.** Movers placed in recent passes count against the cap as phantom sessions for 15 minutes, and nothing else carries over. The floor's per-pass count resets on every call, and the reconciler runs a pass about every 3 seconds. So at 16, up to 15 movers could pile onto the top-ranked account before its burn shows up. That is the second-cascade pattern seen on 2026-09-19.
3. **Where the cap does bite, the session count is the problem, not the number 8.** 63% of tonight's session count on fully capped accounts was subagent transcripts. For heavy movers, the weight rule causes about 154 of 155 modeled wait minutes.

Burst protection stays as it is. Today the live legacy lane allows 2 concurrent recoveries. From the reconciler cutover (the recon.on flag), the first-turn pacer allows 3 per account.

The count and weight fixes are separate items. Revisit the cap only when either of these shows a real storm waiting on it:
- the reconciler in act mode (live, after the cutover) holds a cohort on the cap (reason kmax-concurrency) for more than about 10 minutes, or
- a hook-lane request uses up its 3 attempts with every account excluded by the cap.

The current shadow run cannot show this: it never charges its own placements, so its plans never count against later passes.
